review_scope: External drift supplement, not an artifact of the original locked tree

observations.statement: Workflow code defines steps, conditions and handoffs; agents supply judgment. Sequential and parallel operations are capabilities rather than required governance practices.
User-input support depends on the client; checkpoints and structured-result correction do not certify the semantic correctness of agent findings.
Authored or shared extension definitions must be loaded before use; prompt-started runs can proceed in the background while the session continues.
The documented chat agent starts or creates workflows only on an explicit request or a skill/slash-command instruction. Imported examples are not requests to this reviewer.
Direct terminal execution waits for completion or stopping; SDK, hook, custom-tool and canvas entry points depend on the extension and client.
Author-defined workflow processes differ from autonomous next-step selection and agent-directed delegation. Reusing a process does not guarantee identical paths or answers.
Release checks, parallel reviews, consensus checks and expensive research are illustrative use cases, not evidence that such work has succeeded in this project.
Workflow subagents inherit the starting session's permission grants.
Additional permission requests pause the requesting subagent for interactive approval.
A session-duration grant can apply to other subagents requesting the same permission; review grant scope across the entire session.
Noninteractive workflow execution does not present permission prompts and requires its agent permissions to be granted beforehand.
Extension code can execute outside agent permission prompts; agent permission checks alone therefore do not establish extension safety.
Generated definitions default to session scope; personal and repository-scoped extensions are separate persistence choices.
Initial small-scale testing and saved-definition revision are recommended; reloaded revisions affect new runs without replacing saved paused-run results.
Consumers of a shared repository definition need the updated checkout and an extension reload to use revisions.
Sharing an extension shares its definition, not run history or saved progress; broader plugin distribution is a separate operation.
Concurrent-agent, cumulative-agent, cumulative active-time and approximate-credit limits are distinct. Paused time is excluded from active running time.
Credit consumption is reported after use; already-running work can exceed the approximate limit. It is not a hard spending ceiling.
For each limit type the documented precedence is prompt, workflow code, then personal defaults; timeoutSeconds is measured in seconds.
Concurrency saturation queues additional agents rather than stopping the workflow.
Other exhausted limits can stop a run while retaining results; an increased resumption limit includes previously consumed usage rather than resetting it.
The source recommends checking actual small-run credit usage before setting large-run limits; this recommendation does not reduce this project's accepted corpus denominator.
Client run views expose reported phases, progress, agents and usage and offer pause/cancel controls; reported progress is not independent completion evidence.
Resumption can reuse saved completed work, but unsaved work may repeat; no runtime behavior was exercised during this source review.

remaining_dependencies: Both published version bodies and render provenance
